note: Values copied from primary documents. The HTML files in this directory are local copies of the pages as retrieved on 2026-10-13. They are not in the repository: data-src/reference-copies.json has the address and the SHA-256 of each copy.

voyager2.source: NASA Science, Voyager 2 mission page, https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-2/ (file nasa_voyager2.html)
voyager2.remark: The page gives each distance as a range from the planet (cloud tops). It also states that a course correction occurred two hours after the closest approach to Jupiter.

earth.remark: The page date is the local date in California. The UTC date is 1999-08-18.

cassini.remark: The page gives each distance with the word "about". Venus and Earth: distance from the surface. Jupiter: distance from the planet.

mars2020.source: JPL, Mars 2020 Perseverance Launch Press Kit, https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/mars_2020/launch/mission/ (file jpl_mars2020_presskit.html)
mars2020.source2: NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog, Mars 2020, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=2020-052A (file nssdc_mars2020.html): launch and landing times

travel.quote: it will take 213 days to travel about 309 million miles (497 million kilometers)
travel.remark: The page gives this value for a launch on the first day of the launch period (July 20). Launch time: start of the launch window on July 20 (9:15 a.m. EDT). Landing time: Earth received time of the NSSDCA page minus the signal delay of about 11 minutes.

newhorizons.source: NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog, New Horizons, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=2006-001A (file nssdc_newhorizons.html)
newhorizons.remark: The page says: "within about 32 Jovian radii of Jupiter" and "within 12500 km of Pluto".

insight.source: JPL, InSight Launch Press Kit, Quick Facts (page 14 of the PDF file), https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/insight/launch/download/mars_insight_launch_presskit.pdf

sourceFile.remark: Retrieved on 2026-10-14. The project keeps no copy of this document: the record has the address, the size and the SHA-256 of the file as retrieved.

travel.quote: Travel distance, Earth to Mars (May 5 launch): About 301 million miles (485 million kilometers)
travel.remark: Launch time: start of the launch window on May 5 (11:05 UTC). Landing time: "about noon PST (3 p.m. EST; 20:00 UTC)".

insight.source2: NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog, InSight, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=2018-042A: launch on 5 May 2018 at 11:05 UT, landing on 26 November 2018 at 19:52:59 UT

msl.source: JPL, Mars Science Laboratory Launch Press Kit, Quick Facts (page 6), https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/MSLLaunch.pdf

sourceFile.remark: Retrieved on 2026-10-14. The project keeps no copy of this document: the record has the address, the size and the SHA-256 of the file as retrieved.

travel.quote: Total distance of travel, Earth to Mars: About 354 million miles (570 million kilometers)
travel.remark: The document does not give the launch day of this value. The test uses the first day of the launch period: the document gives the distance between the Earth and Mars for that day. Launch time: first launch opportunity on Nov. 25 (10:25 a.m. EST). Landing time: middle of "Aug. 6, 5 a.m. to 5:30 a.m. Universal Time".

msl.source2: NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog, Mars Science Laboratory, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=2011-070A: launch on 26 November 2011 at 15:02 UT, touchdown at 05:32 UTC on 6 August
msl.source3: Martin-Mur, Kruizinga, Wong, "Mars Science Laboratory Interplanetary Navigation Analysis", ISSFD 2011, page 4, https://www.issfd.org/ISSFD_2011/S6-Interplanetary.Navigation-IN/S6_P3_ISSFD22_PF_001.pdf: the set "Type 1B" has a launch period from November 25, 2011 through December 18, 2011, "with a constant arrival date of August 6, 2012". "The launch/arrival sets are limited by the performance of the launch vehicle and the desired entry velocity at Mars."

phoenix.source: JPL, Phoenix Launch Press Kit, Quick Facts (page 6), https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/phoenix-launch-presskit.pdf

sourceFile.remark: Retrieved on 2026-10-14. The project keeps no copy of this document: the record has the address, the size and the SHA-256 of the file as retrieved.

travel.quote: Total distance traveled, Earth to Mars: About 680 million kilometers (423 million miles)
travel.remark: The document does not give the launch day of this value. The test uses the first day of the launch period: the document gives the distance between the Earth and Mars for that day. Launch time: first launch window on Aug. 3 (5:35 a.m. EDT). The document gives the landing day only: "If launched during first 15 days of launch period, landing May 25, 2008". Landing time: touchdown time of the NSSDCA page.

phoenix.source2: NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog, Phoenix, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=2007-034A: launch on 04 August 2007 at 09:26:34 UT, touchdown at 23:53:44 UT on 25 May
